evidence: High-voltage electrofragmentation/pre-weakening of dunite has been lab-tested for ore comminution (Metals 2022) and pre-weakening cuts grinding energy ~30% in ores, but no work applies it to olivine for enhanced weathering.
1950s patent US2832665 proposes shock-tube heating plus rapid expansion quench for fixing atmospheric nitrogen as NO, and shock-tube N2+O2 kinetics are studied, but no fertilizer device was found.
Searched photocatalytic superhydrophilic glass as a falling-film DAC contactor; found only separate superhydrophilic-glass patents and structured-packing DAC contactors.
Searched SMA/thermally actuated frost covers; found only thermally actuated venting plant covers and spring-deployed seedling covers, nothing that self-deploys a frost cover by SMA.
Swallowable self-expanding gastric devices exist but use balloons or hydrogels (Elipse, Plenity, US8287562); intragastric implants with Nitinol collapsible frames are only patented, not swallowable.

Patents describe temperature-actuated drip valves (US4638828) and a drip outlet with a heat-sensitive spring compensator (RU2282346), plus SMA irrigation/sprinkler valves, but no working sun-heated SMA emitter.

Lab work has made PET nanoparticles by dissolving and anti-solvent precipitation and degraded them enzymatically, and a 2025 Faraday Discussions paper tests dissolution-precipitation as pretreatment for enzymatic PET depolymerization.

Electron-trapping optical memory was built in doped alkaline-earth sulfide phosphors (rewritable, UV/visible-written), and quartz TL under X-rays is studied, but nothing on X-ray-written quartz trap archival storage.
Powered electrostatic fog harvesting is well studied (ion emitters charge the droplets, 50-90% capture in lab tests), but no passive, permanently charged electret net was found.

Patents describe airlock dust-removal systems that neutralize suit dust and trap it in a filter under the astronaut's platform, and NASA tested airlock filtration, but no electret-curtain capture was found.

Electrostatic nets exist but only to hold insecticide/fungal powder (In2Care); a Gates grant proposes a sticky electrically charged net to trap mosquitoes for surveillance; no insecticide-free electret bed net found.
Multiple patents (e.g. US4753573) and a retail product sell electrostatic filter strips stuck to ceiling-fan blades to capture airborne particles, though without measured performance data.

Olfactory-targeted nasal devices exist (Nemera Guided Stream, circumferential-velocity spray patent) and simulations show liquid-film translocation along the wall to the olfactory region, but no Coanda-jet nozzle found.
Searched auxetic/negative-Poisson's-ratio braided sutures; found only conventional cut-through studies and auxetic tendon tissue/scaffold work, no auxetic suture.
A published flow sensor for hydrocephalus shunts uses a flexible flap carrying a permanent magnet that deflects with CSF flow, read through the skin by a commercial magnetic field sensor.

A patent describes a joint-implant cycle counter with a magnet in one component and a Hall switch in the other counting flexion steps (US7347874); Wiegand wires are marketed for implants, but no Wiegand knee counter exists.

Patent US12296867 describes a battery-free on-wheel bearing thermal sensor powered by a magnetic power unit from wheel rotation; Wiegand sensors are used in rail tachometers, but no Wiegand bearing monitor found.

Axion Consulting for WRAP demonstrated diffraction gratings stamped in moulds or onto PP packaging that a laser/camera reads to identify food-contact plastic for sorting, though not deployed commercially.

An electrochromic contact lens covering the pupil is patented (US10678068) and intermittent occlusion is built as Amblyz liquid-crystal glasses, but no electrochromic contact lens for amblyopia was found.

Conference papers propose and FE-model DC conduction and induction electromagnetic pumps for molten salts in solar plants, and an MHD molten-salt pump is patented, but no tested pump in nitrate CSP loops found.
A UC San Diego team built a forearm-worn Peltier cooling device for essential tremor with clinician-set zones (prototype, no patient data); Mayo Clinic tested forearm cooling with cold packs.

A patent application covers hydrophilic coatings for automotive lidar covers to form a uniform water film, and Pao et al. 2024 lab-tested hydrophilic lidar covers in rain, but no photocatalytic/sun-activated version found.
DGIST (2025) built and tested a power-free device whose SMA springs flip wings between a black solar-absorbing face and a radiative-cooling face to heat or cool buildings by temperature.
